# What Does a Pulley Actually Do?

<!-- STEP id="redirects-not-changes" -->
## A Pulley Just Redirects

A pulley is a wheel that a string runs over.

It redirects the string's pull — turns a downward pull into a sideways one, say.

It adds nothing. It removes nothing.

<!-- STEP id="the-idealization" -->
## Smooth and Light

Every pulley in this lesson is **smooth**: frictionless at its axle, so it costs nothing to spin.

Every pulley is also light enough that its own mass barely matters.

The string slides over it as freely as over a frictionless doorknob.

<!-- STEP id="same-tension-throughout" -->
## One Tension, Both Sides

Nothing eats any of the pull along the way.

So the tension is the same number all along that string — from one end, over the pulley, to the other end.

**A smooth, light pulley changes a string's direction. It never changes its tension.**
